observations: Photo 0 shows a large yellow industrial diesel engine assembly with multiple hoses/lines, intake/exhaust components, and an open/removed top area; no clear engine model plate visible.

Photo 1 shows the top/valve cover area of a similar engine with wiring/hoses and a few labels/plates, but the text is not readable enough to confirm model (C9) or make (Caterpillar) from the image alone.
Both photos appear to show an engine with accessories removed/installed, but there is no clear serial/model tag, no close-up of identification, and no visible compression/rotation test evidence.

claims.evidence: Photos show an industrial diesel engine assembly, but the Caterpillar branding and the specific model 'C9' are not readable/confirmable (no clear model/serial plate close-up). Also 'complete' is not verifiable from only two angles.

risks.risk: Model mismatch risk (engine may not be Caterpillar C9; could be another Caterpillar/aftermarket or different displacement).
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the engine data plate/serial plate showing make/model (C9) and serial number, plus a photo of the stamped engine code if present.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic used diesel engine parts/unknown model (worst case: not confirmed C9).

risks.risk: Not actually complete (missing major components like turbo, injectors, alternator, starter, ECM, fuel pump, or wiring harness).
risks.proof: A full parts inventory photo/clip laid out (or a checklist) showing all major components included, and a photo of the engine fully assembled with all external components attached.
risks.if_unproven: Price as incomplete/parts-only (worst case: missing key running components).

risks.risk: Condition/working status unknown (could be seized, damaged, or for parts only).
risks.proof: Video clip of the engine cranking/turning (hand crank or starter) and, if possible, a compression test or leak-down result.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven working (worst case: for parts only).

risks.risk: Compatibility risk (mounting, flywheel housing, intake/exhaust configuration, and electrical connectors may not match the buyer’s application).
risks.proof: Photos of mounting points, flywheel/flexplate side, and connector types; plus the intended application/vehicle/equipment model.
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming compatibility is not guaranteed (worst case: buyer may need extra parts).

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the engine data/serial plate showing Caterpillar model 'C9' and serial number (photo must be readable).
Photos showing all included major components (turbo, injectors, alternator, starter, fuel pump, ECM/ECU, wiring harness, intake/exhaust manifolds) and what is missing.
Video of the engine cranking/turning freely (and ideally a compression test result).
Photos of flywheel/flexplate side and mounting points to confirm compatibility with the buyer’s setup.
response.reason: The photos show a diesel engine assembly, but the specific Caterpillar C9 identity and whether it is complete/working cannot be confirmed from readable model/serial information or test evidence. Without that, a safe worst-case price selection from comparables is not reliable.
